name: sparkl
description: Trading card prices, set lists and values, release dates and price trends from Sparkl's public catalog.

interface.longDescription:
Sparkl helps trading card collectors look up card prices, set values, release dates and daily price changes. Search the public catalog for Pokemon, One Piece, Disney Lorcana, Riftbound, Gundam, Dragon Ball Super Fusion World, Sorcery, Grand Archive and Cyberpunk. Look up a card's price by finish, a set's release date and most valuable cards, upcoming sets, or price risers and fallers. Most-valuable-card rankings are available for Pokemon, One Piece, Lorcana and Riftbound.

Prices are Near Mint, ungraded market references, refreshed daily: TCGplayer in US dollars and Cardmarket in euros, with observation dates and links to the relevant Sparkl pages. An eBay-based estimate is identified as an estimate when returned. Prices are informational and are not guaranteed sale prices.

The MCP connection is public and read-only. No account or API key is needed. It cannot access personal collections, buy or sell cards, provide graded prices, or retrieve sold listings.

prompts: What is Umbreon ex from Prismatic Evolutions worth?
Which Pokémon sets come out next?
Which One Piece cards rose in price today?

positive.description: User prompt: "What is the English Umbreon ex 161/131 from Prismatic Evolutions worth by finish?" Look up a specific English card and its prices by finish using the public catalog; no account or setup is required.
positive.prompt: What is the English Umbreon ex 161/131 from Prismatic Evolutions worth by finish?
positive.expected_behavior: Call search_cards with query identifying Umbreon ex 161/131 and game=pokemon, then get_card with card_id returned for the matching English printing. Report only returned finishes and prices, identifying TCGplayer USD and Cardmarket EUR, observation dates and the Sparkl URL. Explain missing prices without inventing them.

positive.description: User prompt: "What is in the English Pokemon set Prismatic Evolutions, what is its total market value, and what are its most valuable cards?" Read a named set and its aggregate value; use the English printing of Prismatic Evolutions.
positive.prompt: What is in the English Pokemon set Prismatic Evolutions, what is its total market value, and what are its most valuable cards?
positive.expected_behavior: Call get_set with game=pokemon, set=Prismatic Evolutions and language=en. Report the returned release date, card count, aggregate market values and top cards with their source currencies and Sparkl links. Do not imply the returned top cards are the complete set list.

positive.description: User prompt: "Which Pokemon sets are coming out next, and when?" Read upcoming releases for a supported game. Results change over time; an empty result is a valid outcome.
positive.prompt: Which Pokemon sets are coming out next, and when?
positive.expected_behavior: Call upcoming_releases with game=pokemon. List the returned upcoming sets in release-date order, using the returned English release dates and Sparkl links. If none are returned, explain that no upcoming sets are listed instead of fabricating releases.

positive.description: User prompt: "Which One Piece cards rose and fell the most in price today?" Read the latest available daily price movements for One Piece, identifying the date of the data.
positive.prompt: Which One Piece cards rose and fell the most in price today?
positive.expected_behavior: Call price_trends with game=one-piece. Summarize returned rises and falls, current and previous prices, changes and observation date. Identify TCGplayer USD, distinguish any Cardmarket-confirmed 30-day changes from daily moves, and cite Sparkl links. Do not invent data if unavailable.

positive.description: User prompt: "Show me the five most valuable Riftbound cards right now." Read a supported game ranking with a bounded result count.
positive.prompt: Show me the five most valuable Riftbound cards right now.
positive.expected_behavior: Call most_valuable_cards with game=riftbound and limit=5. Return no more than five ranked cards from the response, with their sets, numbers, returned prices, source currencies and Sparkl links. Explain missing data rather than inventing a ranking.

negative.description: User prompt: "Buy me an Umbreon ex for 200 euros using my saved card." Purchases are unsupported. Explain that Sparkl only reads public catalog data; do not invoke any Sparkl tool to execute a purchase and do not claim an order was placed.
negative.prompt: Buy me an Umbreon ex for 200 euros using my saved card.

negative.description: User prompt: "Open my private Sparkl collection and remove all duplicate cards." Private collection access and mutations are unsupported. Do not call Sparkl tools for private account data and do not claim a collection was read or changed.
negative.prompt: Open my private Sparkl collection and remove all duplicate cards.

negative.description: User prompt: "Show the last ten completed eBay sales and PSA 10 price for this Umbreon ex." Graded prices and sold listings are not covered. Explain this limitation without calling Sparkl tools as if they supplied graded valuations or completed sales.
negative.prompt: Show the last ten completed eBay sales and PSA 10 price for this Umbreon ex.

review.commerce_description: The MCP is read-only and does not sell products, place orders or process payments. Its results link to public Sparkl catalog pages; separate website or app services are outside this MCP.

publication.release_notes: Initial OpenAI directory submission with public card search, prices by finish, set information, upcoming releases, price trends and supported card rankings. No authentication required.
